summary: Production entrypoints/counters support a no-product-edit baseline. Full-directory rereads and full-generation JSON are separate costs. Two bounded prototype directions are advisory, not measured or approved.

findings.claim: Benchmark beginOrResumeScanGeneration -> scanSlice -> recordScanSlice, continuing from commit.generation until commit.observation exists. Scanner completion excludes required validation/publication. PerformanceTests lacks this path.
findings.recommendation: Use synthetic roots/DB and fixed inputs. Time scanner and store separately, including nil-observation validation calls and final inclusive publication. Verify durable output, not only inline results capped at 2048. Include initial and unchanged/rescan generations.

findings.claim: Diagnostics expose enumeration passes, inspected entries, peak retained names and change restarts. A static flat D-name directory with budget B inspects roughly D*ceil(D/B) names; processedEntryCount hides rereads. readdir is not cancellation-aware.
findings.recommendation: Sum passes/inspections/restarts, maximize retained names; report work per distinct entry, slice latency distribution and total time. B bounds processed work/heap, not I/O or time. Use external process/time supervision.

findings.claim: No scoped API directly reports cumulative frontier rewrites or pure stage/COMMIT time. progress length gives persisted occupancy. diagnostics() gives DB/WAL/SHM sizes but also runs quick_check/counts. PerformanceTests demonstrates LiveResourceMeasurementSource.measure RSS/CPU/DB bytes.
findings.recommendation: Record frontier count and synthetic-DB length(progress); current bytes are not cumulative writes. A separate instrumented run can sum NEW.progress lengths per write. Use monotonic call timing/existing reconciliationCheckpoint markers; label final time inclusive. Sample peak RSS/WAL through long calls and before close; keep quick_check/count diagnostics outside timed loops.

findings.claim: Generation reads decode full progress; writes re-encode all roots/frontiers. The scanner copies/appends frontier arrays. Each staging call counts distinct paths; validation can rewrite progress again. Enumeration-only changes leave these costs.
findings.recommendation: Use indexed generation/root work rows, bounded dequeue and cursor/child deltas committed with staged metadata, invalidations and scheduler state. Do not rematerialize/serialize the whole queue at the adapter boundary. Measure queue and aggregate-count costs separately.

findings.claim: Two minimal enumeration candidates pair with incremental frontier rows: bounded process-local directory streams, or disk-backed names keyed by root/directory/pass. Handles/opaque offsets alone cannot prove durable restart correctness.
findings.recommendation: A: cap handles, consume successive batches; loss/eviction/restart invalidates unfinished pass/subtree work. B: stream names into bounded DB chunks, page them, charge spool/WAL cost and invalidate on signature change. Both preserve owner-root membership, signature checks, sample times, dirty-token rejection, reopen revalidation and guarded atomic publication.

findings.claim: Flat-file throughput can hide skipped coverage, frontier growth and unfair scheduling. Scope identity includes entry/depth budgets; overlap, exclusions and investigation expiry change required work.
findings.recommendation: Fresh matched DB per B. Cover wide files, empty-directory fanout, branching trees, depth-limit/beyond-limit chains, skewed roots with B<root count, exclusions/symlinks and overlapping roots/hard links with one failed root. Mutate before lexical cursor and after completed passes; replace/delete subtrees; inject same/earlier-time dirty receipt before submitting an old slice. Reopen after staging and during validation; fault publication checkpoints. Assert healthy-root progress, rejected stale publication, no false absence, complete state/events and atomic rollback. Charge recovery work and report capacity failures, not false speedups.
